title: Lighted Magnifiers for Reading Small Print: What to Look For and What They Can't Do
subtitle: A plain-English look at handheld LED magnifiers, and how power and lens size trade off.
excerpt: A lighted magnifier can make small print easier to see. Here is how power and lens size trade off, and what a magnifier cannot fix.
author: Nickel And Gadget Editors

sections.content: Small print turns up in the places that matter most. It is on the side of a prescription bottle, in the fine print of a bill, and on a menu in a dim restaurant.

A lighted magnifier is a simple tool for those moments. It is a lens that makes words look bigger, with a small built-in light that shines on the page. There is no app to learn and nothing to connect. Choosing one mostly comes down to power and lens size.
The power of a magnifier is written as a number followed by an x. A 2x lens makes print look about twice as big. A 5x lens makes it look about five times as big, and so on.

Here is the trade-off. Higher power comes with a smaller lens. Among the Carson Optical models below, the 5x magnifier has a 2.5-inch lens, while the 7x model has a 1.5-inch lens. A smaller lens shows less of the page at once, so the 7x suits a few words at a time rather than whole paragraphs.
You may also see the word aspheric. The seller's page for the Carson 5x describes its lens this way: "Aspheric lens … for better magnification and image clarity."

items: Power and lens size. Higher power means a smaller lens, so think about whether you need a few words at a time or a bigger view.
Batteries. Find out what kind the light uses and whether they come in the box. One lighted magnifier we found, from General Tools, needs 2 AA batteries that are not included.
Shipping costs. MaxiAids, which sells the Carson models below, lists free domestic shipping on web orders over $75.
Steadiness. Handheld magnifiers need a steady hand, so a stand or a soft grip may matter if you have tremor or arthritis. Ask your doctor if you are unsure what suits you.

sections.content: These are listings we found on the makers' and sellers' pages. We have not tested any of these products, and we have not confirmed current prices, so check the price and availability with the seller before you buy.
Good light still helps, even with a lighted model. Sit near a lamp or window when you can. Keep the lens clean with a soft cloth, since smudges blur the view.
A magnifier makes print look bigger. It does not treat or diagnose any eye problem. If you notice sudden or worsening vision changes, see an eye doctor.
sections.label: Good to Know

sections.content: A lighted magnifier will not solve every vision problem, but it can make everyday reading a little less frustrating. Think about the print you read most, and pick the power and lens size to match.
